findings.explanation: Splunkbase 4022 is 'Technical Addon for the Metricator application for Nmon (HEC)' and 6876 is 'Network Monitoring App'. Neither is a Cisco ACI or Nexus add-on. Both IDs are repeated in dataSources, detailedImplementation and references.
findings.suggested_fix: Remove 4022 and 6876. For APIC/NX-OS corroboration, cite Cisco DC Networking (7777), which collects ACI, Nexus 9000 and Nexus Dashboard data, and an NX-OS syslog path such as SC4S.

findings.explanation: NDI anomalies are alert/finding records with category, severity and object fields. They are not flow or session records, so Network_Traffic does not fit. The detailedImplementation justifies the mapping with 'CRCs, link flaps… mapped to Network_Traffic stories', which is the link-state mismatch the CIM model is not meant for.
findings.suggested_fix: Keep Alerts only and remove Network_Traffic, together with the matching sentence in detailedImplementation.

findings.explanation: The SPL block inside detailedImplementation contains markdown bold markers (**anomaly_key**, **site_label**, **firstSeenTimestamp**), so a copy-paste will not run and no longer matches the spl field. Garbled fragments such as '****Splunk Help** TLS**' and '**Splunk **SOC****' also appear.
findings.suggested_fix: Paste the SPL verbatim from the spl field with no markup, and remove the broken bold fragments.

findings.explanation: I could not confirm that NDI has a native Splunk/HEC streaming target. NDI export options are documented as Kafka message bus, email and syslog, so the HEC webhook path may not exist as written.
findings.quote: Enable **NDI Settings** → System Settings → External Streaming → Splunk targeting **HTTP Event Collector** endpoints on 443/tcp
findings.suggested_fix: Check the Nexus Dashboard Insights 6.x 'Export Data' documentation and describe the supported export types, for example syslog to SC4S or Kafka into Splunk Connect for Kafka.

findings.explanation: The six named dashboards are attributed to the Cisco DC Networking app without evidence. The app description only mentions a default dashboard plus anomaly and advisory views.
findings.quote: (1) Splunkbase **7777** — **Anomaly Volume by Severity** with **`sev_lc`** overlays
findings.suggested_fix: Confirm the panel names in the 7777 app, or describe the panels generically.

findings.explanation: 'NDA1100' and 'NDA-K9' do not match the Nexus Dashboard appliance PIDs I know (SE-NODE-G2, ND-NODE-L4, ND-NODE-G5S).
findings.suggested_fix: Check the Nexus Dashboard hardware data sheet and list the correct appliance PIDs.

findings.explanation: The UC is marked verified by an agent reviewer despite wrong Splunkbase IDs and unconfirmed export mechanics.
The user guide reference points at the cisco.com root, and the 4022 reference is mislabelled as 'Splunk Add-on for Cisco ACI'.
findings.quote:
"title": "Cisco Nexus Dashboard Insights User Guide, Release 6.4",
      "url": "https://www.cisco.com/c/en/us/"
findings.suggested_fix: Link the NDI 6.4 user guide directly and drop the 4022 and 6876 references.

firewalled_field_flags.issue: 'dc(site_label) as sites_impacted' is computed while grouping BY site_label, so it is always 1. In hotspot, the description-based branches (pfc, crc, contract) can only run when the category is not one of the five matched first, so 'physical_crc' never fires for connectivity anomalies. There is no severity or count threshold, so every active anomaly is returned.

summary: The core NDI anomaly roll-up is usable, but the UC cites two Splunkbase IDs that belong to unrelated apps and maps NDI anomalies to Network_Traffic. The detailedImplementation copy of the SPL is corrupted by markdown bold markers. Several export, dashboard and hardware claims are unverified.
